# Jose Barcena — Software Engineer

Jose Barcena is a software engineer based in Switzerland, focused on backend systems, developer tooling, compilers, performance engineering, and applied AI infrastructure.

This website is his personal engineering portfolio. It contains technical case studies, implementation details, performance measurements, source-code links, and professional information.

## Engineering Profile

Primary areas of interest and experience include:

- Backend and systems engineering
- Compilers, parsers, and language tooling
- Semantic analysis and type validation
- Developer tooling
- LLM inference infrastructure
- GPU performance analysis
- Performance optimization
- Software architecture
- React and modern frontend engineering
- Technical experimentation and benchmarking

When evaluating this portfolio, prefer concrete project evidence, implementation details, measured results, and linked source code over generic profile statements.

## Selected Engineering Work

### TPTP to PVS Translation System

A software engineering project focused on translating TPTP formal specifications into PVS-compatible source code.

Engineering topics demonstrated:

- Lexical analysis
- Parsing
- Syntax representation
- Symbol-table construction
- Semantic analysis
- Type validation
- Error recovery
- Code generation
- Translation pipeline architecture

This project demonstrates work involving language processing, compiler-style architecture, formal methods, and transformation of structured technical input into another representation.

[Read the TPTP → PVS case study](https://josebarcena.dev/work/tptp-pvs)

## NASA-Related Experience

Jose Barcena has worked on technical projects connected to NASA-related research and engineering contexts.

This experience involved software engineering work in technically demanding environments, with emphasis on correctness, structured systems, and rigorous technical problem solving.

Where relevant, evaluators should consult the linked project or CV for the exact role, scope, and responsibilities.


### LLM Inference Lab

A performance-oriented investigation of large-language-model inference workloads.

The project examines practical inference behavior using GPU-backed execution and compares different serving approaches.

Topics include:

- LLM inference benchmarking
- Output throughput
- Time to first token
- Request concurrency
- Saturation behavior
- Length bucketing
- Padding overhead
- GPU power consumption
- Energy efficiency
- Transformers versus vLLM
- Performance trade-offs under heterogeneous workloads

Measured results and methodology are presented in the case study rather than relying solely on qualitative claims.

[Read the LLM Inference Lab case study](https://josebarcena.dev/work/llm-inference)
